newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Over 100,000 Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia without valid work permits face deportation as Kua Lalampur's deadline of a four-month amnesty to have their jobs regularised expires on December 31.
Unidentified assailants on Wednesday gunned down a top pro-peace tribal leader in Rangamati hill district.
Members of Parliament (MPs) will get office space, staff support and equipment like a computer under a project aimed at increasing institutional strength of the legislature.

Opposition leader and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia who retunred home Wednessay after a medical treatment in Saudi Arabia said her Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) would soon launch strong movement against "autocratic activities" of the government.
At least 20 million people in 15 districts are suffering from skin diseases caused by arsenic pollution of sub-soil water, a seminar was told in Dhaka on Wednesday.
Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad has termed the water accrod with India a big "diplomatic success" of the Awami League government.
Bangladesh might lose the Generalised System of Preference (GSP) in exporting knitwear specially in European countries following complaint of using imported yarn instead of indigenous one.
Beach Hatchery Ltd, a joint venture project with Taiwan, has been launched at Teknaf aiming to meet the huge shortfall of shrimp fry.
